questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explain: A vector has both magnitude and direction. Velocity has direction, so it is a vector; mass, temperature and speed are scalars (magnitude only).

questions.q: Which of these is a non-contact force?
questions.explain: A non-contact force acts without objects touching. Gravitational force acts at a distance; friction, air resistance and tension all require contact.

questions.q: Two forces act on a box along the same line: 12 N to the right and 7 N to the left. What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
questions.explain: Forces along the same line subtract when opposite: resultant = 12 − 7 = 5 N (acting to the right).

questions.q: A person pushes a trolley with a force of 30 N and moves it 8.0 m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done.
questions.explain: W = Fs = 30 × 8.0 = 240 J. One joule is the work done when 1 N moves through 1 m.

questions.q: A spring has a spring constant of 25 N/m. Calculate the force needed to extend it by 0.20 m (within the limit of proportionality).
questions.explain: F = ke = 25 × 0.20 = 5 N. Force is proportional to extension for an elastic spring within its limit of proportionality.

questions.q: Calculate the weight of a 6.0 kg object on Earth (gravitational field strength g = 9.8 N/kg).
questions.explain: W = mg = 6.0 × 9.8 = 58.8 N. Weight is the force of gravity on the mass.

questions.q: An object has a resultant force of zero acting on it. What can you conclude?
options: It is either stationary or moving at constant velocity
questions.explain: Zero resultant force means no acceleration, so the object stays still or keeps moving at constant velocity (Newton's first law).

questions.q: Work is done on an object when a force makes it move. What energy transfer often warms the surroundings when work is done against friction?
options: Energy is transferred to the thermal store, raising temperature
Energy is destroyed by the friction
questions.explain: Work done against friction transfers energy to the thermal store of the object and surroundings, so they warm up. Energy is conserved, not created or destroyed.

questions.q: What does it mean if a spring is stretched beyond its limit of proportionality?
options: The extension is no longer directly proportional to the force
No more force is needed to stretch it
questions.explain: Beyond the limit of proportionality the force–extension graph is no longer a straight line, so extension is no longer directly proportional to force (and deformation may become inelastic).

questions.q: Two forces act on an object in the same direction: 15 N and 9 N. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force.
questions.explain: Forces in the same direction add: resultant = 15 + 9 = 24 N.

questions.q: A spacecraft component has a mass of 12 kg. Calculate its weight on the Moon, where the gravitational field strength is 1.6 N/kg.
questions.explain: W = mg = 12 × 1.6 = 19.2 N. The mass stays the same anywhere, but weight depends on the local gravitational field strength.

questions.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: They are the same thing measured in different units
Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on it (N)
Weight is measured in kilograms; mass in newtons
Mass changes with location; weight does not
questions.explain: Mass is the quantity of matter in an object, measured in kilograms, and is the same everywhere. Weight is the gravitational force on that mass, measured in newtons, and depends on the gravitational field strength.

questions.q: A crane lifts a load by doing 1800 J of work to raise it 3.0 m. Calculate the force applied.
questions.explain: Rearranging W = Fs gives F = W/s = 1800 / 3.0 = 600 N.

questions.q: A force of 250 N pushes a box and does 1000 J of work. Calculate the distance the box moves in the direction of the force.
questions.explain: Rearranging W = Fs gives s = W/F = 1000 / 250 = 4 m.

questions.q: A force of 6.0 N stretches a spring by 0.15 m within its limit of proportionality. Calculate the spring constant.
questions.explain: Rearranging F = ke gives k = F/e = 6.0 / 0.15 = 40 N/m.

questions.q: On a free-body diagram of a book resting on a table, which two forces are shown acting on the book?
options: Weight downward and the normal contact (reaction) force upward
questions.explain: The book's weight acts downward and the table pushes up with an equal normal contact (reaction) force. As they balance, the resultant force is zero and the book stays still.

questions.q: A car drives along a straight road at a steady speed. What does this tell you about the forces on it?
options: The driving force is greater than the resistive forces
The forces are balanced, giving zero resultant force
questions.explain: Steady speed in a straight line means constant velocity, so by Newton's first law the resultant force is zero — the driving force balances friction and air resistance.

questions.q: Hooke's law states that, up to the limit of proportionality, the extension of a spring is:
options: Directly proportional to the force applied
questions.explain: Hooke's law: extension is directly proportional to the force, so F = ke. This holds only up to the limit of proportionality, beyond which the relationship is no longer linear.
